Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification - Nova Retail

Hi Jamie / Taylor -

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed so everyone is aligned:

Summary of SLOs you asked us to qualify against:
- Latency: P95 end-to-end generation <= 150 ms for typical prompts (avg generation ~40 tokens).
- Throughput: steady-state 200 requests/sec, with burst to ~300 rps during promotions.
- Concurrency: support 300 concurrent active sessions (user-facing connections).
- Streaming: token-by-token streaming required (SSE/WebSocket) with per-token latency ideally <50 ms.
- Availability target: 99.9% monthly for the inference path.

Key constraints you flagged:
- Strict data residency (US only) - we will run in our us-west region.
- No PII in model training; only runtime inference on hashed user ids.

What we'll do next (agreed items):
1) We'll run a perf qualification with a sample traffic file you provided (please confirm the CSV format - attached one is what we used during the call).
2) Redwood infra (Rishi + Neha) will evaluate cost/perf levers: continuous batching, prefix/KV caching, quantization profile, and a recommended model variant set for your latency targets.
3) Draft SLA and acceptance criteria (attached draft SLA).
4) Schedule a 45-min follow-up to walk the perf results and recommended config.

Rishi, can you outline an initial config we should try on the perf run (batching window, quantization, model variant)? Jamie/Taylor - if those SLO numbers look right, confirm and we'll book the perf run for Monday.

Thanks,

 - Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification - Nova Retail

Thanks Marissa - added a few technical notes we should include in the perf run so the numbers are representative. Quick suggestions:

Traffic shape we need from Nova for the run:
- 90% short prompts (~20 tokens gen), 10% long (~120 tokens).
- Inter-arrival distribution with occasional burst windows (30s at 2x baseline QPS).

Initial perf config (what I'll spin up):
- Model variant: redwood-v1-medium (13B-ish equivalent) + fallback to redwood-v1-small for non-critical routes. We'll also try a 4-bit quantized build for cost comparison.
- Quantization profile: 4-bit weight-quant + FP16 activations (best latency/cost tradeoff).
- Continuous batching: 8-12 ms micro-batching window for user-facing latency targets; enable adaptive batching to grow batch size under high QPS.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching with 30-minute TTL for repeated prefixes (expect 10-25% token savings on customer traffic).
- Concurrency and workers: start with 16 worker shards per GPU with 2 GPUs for baseline; we can scale to 4 GPUs for burst if needed.
- Streaming: enable token streaming via SSE with internal per-token pipeline parallelism to keep per-token latency <50 ms.

Cost levers to report in the run:
- Quantized vs FP16 perf + cost delta (tokens/sec and $/1M tokens).
- Batch window tuning (latency vs cost curve).
- Cache hit rate sensitivity (0%–40% scenarios).
- Model mix (medium + small fallback) to show availability vs cost tradeoff.

Deliverables for Monday: perf-run report (latency histograms, P50/P95/P99, tokens/sec, cost estimate), recommended config, and a short deck with tradeoffs. I'll need the confirmed sample traffic (CSV) by EOD Sunday.

 - Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Systems Engineer, Inference Runtime
rishi@redwood.ai

From: Jamie Collins <jamie.collins@nova-retail.com>

Appreciate the recap - numbers look reasonable. A couple clarifications:

- P95: we can target 150 ms for the majority of interactive flows, but for multi-turn sessions with 120-token generations we can accept P95 up to 250 ms. Can you show both in the perf outputs?
- Streaming: must be token-by-token, yes. We measure UX by time-to-first-token and per-token latency; both matter.
- Traffic sample: I made a small tweak to the CSV to reflect real-world jitter and sent the file back (attached as nova-perf-sample-traffic.csv).
- Security note: we'll redline any request headers that could carry PII - we'll pass a sanitized sample payload during the run.

When can you run the perf? Monday morning PST would be ideal - if you can't start until Monday afternoon, let us know. Also, can you include an initial cost estimate for sustained 200 rps (monthly volume estimate attached in the CSV comments)?

Thanks - Jamie
